main_answer_reason: The report substantively reconstructs the competing lower-court termination classifications, their notice rationales, several historical relief and waiver events, and discretionary refusal. It also identifies the narrowed Supreme Court appeal and its two substantive questions. However, it omits the original 1863 lease and changing rent terms, important 1934 acquisition interests, the distinct earlier plaintiff appeal, several material 1938 defences, nearly all competing 1941 payment and demand allegations, and essential conditions of the supplied statutory frameworks. Its coverage of permanent tenancy and the parties' factual positions is therefore materially incomplete.
